newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iranian envoy in anti-Israel row to leave Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iranian envoy in anti-Israel row to leave Turkey.

text.p: Iran's ambassador to Turkey, at the centre of a diplomatic row over an anti-Israel rally in Ankara, is to leave the country, a government MP said on Thursday.

But Oguzhan Asilturk told the Anatolian news agency envoy Mohammed Reza Bagheri's departure had nothing to do with the event last Friday that resulted in the arrest of the district mayor who organised it.

"His mission has came to an end. He was leaving anyway," the state-run agency quoted Asilturk, a senior member of the Islamist Welfare Party, as saying. He did not say when the ambassador would leave.

The Turkish foreign ministry protested to Iran this week after the ambassador spoke at the "Jerusalem Night" rally in Ankara along with the district mayor. The speeches were blasted by Turkish media as a call for Islamic sharia law.
Anatolian quoted a foreign ministry official as saying Ankara was also considering a protest against Iran's consul in Istanbul for noting Turks made up the crowd applauding the ambassador's speech.
The main opposition Motherland Party has asked the government to explain the conduct of the Iranian ambassador. The media are asking why Bagheri is still in Turkey.
Welfare party leader Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, visited Iran soon after forming a ruling coalition with a conservative party in June.
